title: Keep the Heroes Out! or Murder Hoboes Plunder no More!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aUWIhJE2n4

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at Keep the Heroes Out!, a cooperative deck-building dungeon defence game sent by the publisher. You play the monsters, fending off guild adventurers who've decided your home is fair game. The factions are the dragon, lizardfolk, ratkin, witches, imps, poltergeists, slimes, nulls and skeletons. Each has its own ten-card starting deck and meeples, and he plays solo as the skeletons.

He sets up the Witch's Cauldron, the first of twenty scenarios, where the resident witch demands frogs for her stew. Some rooms generate bones, books, frogs and coins, and others trade them for cards: frogs for potions, books for spells, bones for new monsters and gold for weapons. A workshop builds traps. The guild deck spawns heroes by room icon, with scenario cards shuffled in. You win by surviving two passes through it, and lose the moment enough heroes stand in the vault to plunder it.

A sample turn shows how fast it swings. He clears every hero from the board, then two archers each shoot a skeleton, the newly active heroes cut down two more, and wizards charge through to the vault. Wizards can also spring a whole jail-cell horde at once. The Guild Master's Revenge expansion adds hero meeples and a one-versus-many mode. It looks like a kids' game, he says, but it's not, and it's going to his pub meetup.

----

Keep the Heroes Out! flips the crawl so you're the dungeon. Do you enjoy playing the monsters, or does it lose something without heroes to root for?
